0.title: The Household of God
0.overview:
Many Christians today think of church as optional, a helpful resource for their personal faith, to be used when convenient. Some have been hurt by churches and keep their distance. Others move from church to church looking for the right music or programmes. Yet the New Testament speaks of the church in the highest terms. It is the church of God, which he obtained with his own blood (Acts 20:28). Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her (Eph 5:25). To love Christ is to love what he loves.

The church is not a building, a denomination or a weekly event. It is a people: those whom God has called out of the world to belong to Christ and to each other. And it is not an invention of Christians. Jesus said, I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it (Matt 16:18). It is his project, and it cannot fail.

This study asks what the church is, why belonging matters, how it is led, what baptism and the Lord's Supper mean, and how a church keeps its purity, unity and mission. On the points where Christians disagree (church government, baptism and the Lord's Supper), the main views are set out before a verdict is given.

Six units: (1) What Is the Church?; (2) Belonging: Why Every Christian Needs a Church; (3) Shepherds and Servants: Elders and Deacons; (4) Baptism; (5) The Lord's Supper; (6) Purity, Unity and Mission. The Worship and the Lord's Day study covers what happens when the church gathers on Sunday.

1.title: What Is the Church?
1.overview:
The New Testament uses many pictures for the church, and each shows something different.

A people. But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his own possession, that you may proclaim the excellencies of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light (1 Pet 2:9). Peter takes titles given to Israel at Sinai (Exod 19:5-6) and applies them to the church of Jews and Gentiles together. The church is the continuation and fulfilment of God's people through the ages.

A family. Believers are members of the household of God (Eph 2:19). God is our Father, Christ is our elder brother, and other believers are our brothers and sisters. This is not sentimental language. It means real obligations: love, care, honesty and loyalty.

A body. Now you are the body of Christ and individually members of it (1 Cor 12:27). Christ is the head; believers are the members, each with a different function, all needing each other.

A temple. The church is a holy temple in the Lord, a dwelling place for God by the Spirit (Eph 2:21-22). God's presence, once found in the temple in Jerusalem, now dwells in his gathered people.

A bride. Christ loves the church as a husband loves his wife, and is preparing her for the wedding day, that he might present the church to himself in splendor, without spot or wrinkle (Eph 5:27).

The universal and the local church. The universal church is all true believers of every time and place, known fully only to God. The local church is a particular gathering of believers in one place, committed to one another under Christ. Most New Testament uses of "church" refer to local congregations: the church in Corinth, the church that meets in a house. You cannot belong to the universal church in practice except by belonging to a local one.
1.theology:
Visible and invisible: The church as God sees it consists of all the elect, all who truly belong to Christ. The church as we see it consists of those who profess faith. These overlap but are not identical. Some who profess are not genuine (1 John 2:19), and the church on earth is always a mixture. This is why the church must exercise care, but cannot read hearts.

Marks of a true church: The Reformers asked how to recognise a true church amid corruption. They answered with three marks: the faithful preaching of the word of God, the right administration of baptism and the Lord's Supper, and the exercise of church discipline. A church without these may have a building and a crowd, but it lacks what makes a church a church.

Israel and the church: The church does not replace Israel as if God had changed plans. Believing Gentiles are grafted into the one olive tree of God's people (Rom 11:17-24). The church is the one people of God, now made up of Jew and Gentile together in Christ.
1.examples:
Then: Saul of Tarsus was persecuting Christians when the risen Jesus stopped him on the road to Damascus and asked, Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? (Acts 9:4). Not "my people," but "me." Christ so identifies with his church that to harm it is to harm him.

Now: A young professional has watched online sermons for two years without attending a church. She thinks of herself as a committed Christian. Reading Ephesians, she realises that the pictures are all corporate: a body, a household, a temple. She cannot be a hand cut off from the body. She starts attending a local church, and within months finds the friendship and accountability she did not know she was missing.

A simple test: If your church disappeared tomorrow, would anyone notice you were missing? Would you miss them?

verseByVerse.quote: He said to them, "But who do you say that I am?" Simon Peter replied, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God." And Jesus answered him, "Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah! For flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven. And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter confesses that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God. Jesus responds by promising to build his church. The church rests on the truth Peter confessed, and on the apostolic witness he gave. Jesus calls it my church. It belongs to him, he builds it and he guarantees it: not even the gates of hell will overcome it.

verseByVerse.quote: So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God, built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus himself being the cornerstone, in whom the whole structure, being joined together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord. In him you also are being built together into a dwelling place for God by the Spirit. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul uses three pictures in quick succession: a nation (fellow citizens), a family (members of the household of God) and a building (a holy temple). Gentiles who were once strangers are now insiders. The temple is still growing. Every believer is a stone being fitted into place, and Christ is the cornerstone that holds it all together.

verseByVerse.quote: As you come to him, a living stone rejected by men but in the sight of God chosen and precious, you yourselves like living stones are being built up as a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. For it stands in Scripture: "Behold, I am laying in Zion a stone, a cornerstone chosen and precious, and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame." So the honor is for you who believe, but for those who do not believe, "The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone," and "A stone of stumbling, and a rock of offense." They stumble because they disobey the word, as they were destined to do. But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his own possession, that you may proclaim the excellencies of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light. Once you were not a people, but now you are God's people; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter calls believers living stones, built into a spiritual house around Christ, the living stone. They are also priests, offering spiritual sacrifices. Then he heaps up Israel's titles and applies them to the church. The purpose is mission: to proclaim the excellencies of God. Those who were once not a people are now God's people.

verseByVerse.quote: For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so it is with Christ. For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body—Jews or Greeks, slaves or free—and all were made to drink of one Spirit. For the body does not consist of one member but of many. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The church at Corinth was divided by rivalries and spiritual pride. Paul reminds them that they are one body, made one by the Spirit. Jews and Greeks, slaves and free: all were baptised into one body and drink of one Spirit. Unity in the church is not something we create. It is something the Spirit has created, which we must keep.

1.reflection:
Which picture of the church (people, family, body, temple, bride) speaks most to you, and why?

What is the difference between the universal and the local church? Why do both matter?

Read Acts 9:1-5. What does it tell you about how Christ sees his church?

How would you explain to a friend why church is not optional for a Christian?

2.title: Belonging: Why Every Christian Needs a Church
2.overview:
The first Christians did not attend church; they belonged to it. After Pentecost, those who believed were baptised and added to the church (Acts 2:41). And they devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers (Acts 2:42). Their faith was immediately corporate.

Why church membership? The phrase "church membership" is not found in the Bible, but the reality is everywhere. The New Testament assumes that believers are known and counted in local churches. Paul writes to particular churches. Elders are told to shepherd the flock of God that is among you (1 Pet 5:2), so they must know who is in it. Church discipline requires knowing who is inside and who is outside (1 Cor 5:12-13). The "one another" commands (love, bear with, encourage, admonish, serve) need specific people to obey them with. Membership is simply making visible a commitment that the New Testament assumes.

What belonging gives. A church gives us teaching we would not choose for ourselves, so that we hear the whole counsel of God. It gives us people who know us well enough to encourage and warn us. It gives us a place to use our gifts. It gives us shepherds who watch over our souls (Heb 13:17). And it gives us the sacraments, which belong to the gathered church.

What belonging asks. It asks faithfulness in attendance: not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another (Heb 10:25). It asks service, giving, prayer and patience with imperfect people. It asks humility to receive correction and submit to godly leaders. It asks us to stay through difficult seasons rather than moving on at the first disappointment.

Choosing a church. Look first for the marks of a true church: is the Bible faithfully taught? Is the gospel clear? Are baptism and the Lord's Supper rightly practised? Are the leaders qualified and accountable? Is there real care for members? Music style, programmes and convenience matter far less. No church is perfect. If you find one, joining it will spoil it.
2.theology:
"Outside the church there is no salvation"? This old saying has been misused to mean that a particular institution controls salvation. That is false; salvation is through faith in Christ alone. But it expresses a truth: God saves people into a people. A believer who deliberately refuses fellowship with other believers is acting against the nature of the new life he has received (1 John 4:20).

When should you leave a church? Serious reasons include the abandonment of the gospel, persistent false teaching, unrepentant abuse by leaders that the church will not address, or a move to another place. Preferences about style are not good reasons. When leaving, do so honestly and peaceably, speaking to the leaders rather than slipping away.

Online church: Recorded sermons can be a blessing to the housebound and to those far from a faithful church. But they cannot replace the gathered body, where believers see, serve, encourage and are known by one another.
2.examples:
Then: In Jerusalem, believers shared their possessions so that there was not a needy person among them (Acts 4:34). Their belonging was not merely a name on a list. It showed in their wallets, their homes and their time.

Now: A couple has moved churches four times in eight years, each time because something disappointed them. Reading Hebrews 10:24-25, they realise they have treated church as a consumer product. They commit to their current church, join a small group, start serving with the children and resolve to raise concerns with the elders directly instead of leaving. Five years later they are among its most valued members.

A simple test: Who in your church knows you well enough to warn you if you were drifting from Christ?

verseByVerse.quote: So those who received his word were baptized, and there were added that day about three thousand souls. And they devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers. And awe came upon every soul, and many wonders and signs were being done through the apostles. And all who believed were together and had all things in common. And they were selling their possessions and belongings and distributing the proceeds to all, as any had need. And day by day, attending the temple together and breaking bread in their homes, they received their food with glad and generous hearts, praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord added to their number day by day those who were being saved. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: This is the earliest snapshot of a local church. Believers were baptised and added. They gave themselves to four things: teaching, fellowship, the Lord's Supper and prayer. They shared generously, met daily and praised God. And the Lord added to their number day by day those who were being saved. Growth was the Lord's work through a devoted, loving community.

verseByVerse.quote: Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for he who promised is faithful. And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day drawing near. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The writer joins three exhortations: hold fast to hope, stir one another up to love and good works, and do not neglect meeting together. They belong together. Christians who drift from the gathered church usually drift from hope and good works as well. We need others to keep us going, and they need us.

verseByVerse.quote: Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they are keeping watch over your souls, as those who will have to give an account. Let them do this with joy and not with groaning, for that would be of no advantage to you. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Church leaders are keeping watch over your souls, as those who will have to give an account. That is a sobering responsibility. Members are called to obey and submit to them so that their work is a joy rather than a burden. This assumes that leaders know who they are responsible for, and that members know whom they are under.

verseByVerse.quote: For as in one body we have many members, and the members do not all have the same function, so we, though many, are one body in Christ, and individually members one of another. Having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us, let us use them: if prophecy, in proportion to our faith; if service, in our serving; the one who teaches, in his teaching; the one who exhorts, in his exhortation; the one who contributes, in generosity; the one who leads, with zeal; the one who does acts of mercy, with cheerfulness. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul uses the body picture again. Many members, different functions, one body. Each believer has gifts, and each is to use them: prophesying, serving, teaching, encouraging, giving, leading, showing mercy. None is too small. A church works best when every member serves, not when a few professionals do everything.

2.reflection:
Are you a member of a local church? If not, what is holding you back?

Read Acts 2:42-47. Which of these marks is strongest in your church, and which is weakest?

What do you give to your church, and what do you receive from it?

What would it mean for you to be more committed to your church this year?

3.title: Shepherds and Servants: Elders and Deacons
3.overview:
Christ, the head of the church, gives it leaders to care for it. The New Testament names two ongoing offices: elders (also called overseers or pastors) and deacons.

Elders. Elders are shepherds. Paul told the Ephesian elders, Pay careful attention to yourselves and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to care for the church of God (Acts 20:28). Their main tasks are to teach the word, to pray, to guard the church from false teaching and to watch over its members. They are to lead not domineering over those in your charge, but being examples to the flock (1 Pet 5:3). They answer to the Chief Shepherd, who will reward faithful service (1 Pet 5:4).

Qualifications. Paul's lists in 1 Timothy 3 and Titus 1 are striking. Almost all the qualifications are about character: above reproach, faithful in marriage, self-controlled, hospitable, gentle, not quarrelsome, not a lover of money, managing his household well, well thought of by outsiders. Only one is about skill: able to teach. Churches often choose leaders for their success or charisma. God chooses them for their godliness.

Plurality. In the New Testament, churches were led by a group of elders, not a single pastor (Acts 14:23; Titus 1:5; Jas 5:14). Some elders labour especially in preaching and teaching (1 Tim 5:17), but all share in the oversight. A plurality guards against the dangers of one man's blind spots and pride.

Deacons. In Acts 6, the apostles appointed seven men to care for neglected widows, so that the apostles could devote themselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word (Acts 6:4). Deacons are servants who lead in practical care, freeing elders to shepherd. Their qualifications are also mainly about character (1 Tim 3:8-13).

Male elders. Scripture restricts the office of elder to qualified men (1 Tim 2:12; 3:2). This is not because women are less gifted or less valuable, but because of God's design for the church family, grounded in creation (1 Tim 2:13). The Biblical Manhood and Biblical Womanhood studies explore this further.
3.theology:
Church government: the views. Episcopal churches are governed by bishops over many congregations. Presbyterian churches are governed by elders, with local elders accountable to regional and national assemblies. Congregational churches are self-governing, with the members holding final authority under Christ, often led by elders.

The verdict: The New Testament pattern is a plurality of qualified elders leading each local church, with the congregation involved in key decisions. The church chose the seven in Acts 6:3, and it is the church that acts in discipline (Matt 18:17; 1 Cor 5:4). Churches also rightly cooperate with one another for counsel and mission, as at the Jerusalem council (Acts 15). The fixed points are that Christ is the head, Scripture is the rule, and leaders must be qualified and accountable.

Pray for your leaders: Elders are sinners like everyone else, and they carry a heavy burden. Paul repeatedly asked churches to pray for him (Eph 6:19; Col 4:3). Encourage your leaders, pray for them and bring concerns to them directly.
3.examples:
Then: When Paul said farewell to the Ephesian elders, he reminded them that he had served with tears, taught publicly and from house to house, and not coveted anyone's silver or gold. Then he knelt and prayed with them, and they all wept (Acts 20:37). This is what shepherding looks like.

Now: A church is choosing new elders. One candidate is a successful businessman and confident speaker, but harsh with his family and known for a quick temper. Another is a quiet schoolteacher whose household is peaceful and who has faithfully taught a Bible study for years. Reading 1 Timothy 3 together, the church sees which one Scripture points to.

A simple test: When did you last pray by name for the elders of your church?

verseByVerse.quote: Pay careful attention to yourselves and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to care for the church of God, which he obtained with his own blood. I know that after my departure fierce wolves will come in among you, not sparing the flock; and from among your own selves will arise men speaking twisted things, to draw away the disciples after them. Therefore be alert, remembering that for three years I did not cease night or day to admonish every one with tears. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul gives the elders their charge. Watch yourselves first, then the flock. Remember that the Spirit made you overseers, and that the church was bought with God's own blood. Then he warns them: wolves will come, from outside and from within. Guarding the flock against false teaching is one of the elder's most important tasks.

verseByVerse.quote: The saying is trustworthy: If anyone aspires to the office of overseer, he desires a noble task. Therefore an overseer must be above reproach, the husband of one wife, sober-minded, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach, not a drunkard, not violent but gentle, not quarrelsome, not a lover of money. He must manage his own household well, with all dignity keeping his children submissive, for if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how will he care for God's church? He must not be a recent convert, or he may become puffed up with conceit and fall into the condemnation of the devil. Moreover, he must be well thought of by outsiders, so that he may not fall into disgrace, into a snare of the devil. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The office of overseer is a noble task. But it requires a proven character. The list is not a demand for perfection, but for maturity and a good reputation. Notice the emphasis on the home: a man who cannot care for his own household cannot care for God's church. And a recent convert should not be appointed, lest he become proud.

verseByVerse.quote: So I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, as well as a partaker in the glory that is going to be revealed: shepherd the flock of God that is among you, exercising oversight, not under compulsion, but willingly, as God would have you; not for shameful gain, but eagerly; not domineering over those in your charge, but being examples to the flock. And when the chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the unfading crown of glory. Likewise, you who are younger, be subject to the elders. Clothe yourselves, all of you, with humility toward one another, for "God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter, an apostle, calls himself a fellow elder. He tells elders to shepherd willingly, not for money and not as tyrants, but as examples. Then he tells younger members to be subject to the elders, and everyone to put on humility. Healthy churches need humble leaders and humble members.

verseByVerse.quote: Now in these days when the disciples were increasing in number, a complaint by the Hellenists arose against the Hebrews because their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution. And the twelve summoned the full number of the disciples and said, "It is not right that we should give up preaching the word of God to serve tables. Therefore, brothers, pick out from among you seven men of good repute, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we will appoint to this duty. But we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word." And what they said pleased the whole gathering, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch. These they set before the apostles, and they prayed and laid their hands on them. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The first serious problem in the church was a complaint of neglect. The apostles did not ignore it, but they did not abandon prayer and preaching to fix it. They asked the church to choose seven men full of the Spirit and wisdom. Practical care matters so much that it required spiritual men. And the result was that the word continued to spread (Acts 6:7).

3.reflection:
Why do you think almost all the qualifications for elders are about character?

What are the benefits of a plurality of elders over a single pastor?

How can you encourage and support the leaders of your church?

Read 1 Peter 5:1-5. What does it ask of leaders, and what of members?

4.title: Baptism
4.overview:
Jesus' last command to his disciples included baptism: Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you (Matt 28:19-20). Baptism is not optional for Christians. It is the Lord's command and the sign of entry into his church.

What baptism means. Baptism pictures union with Christ in his death and resurrection: We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life (Rom 6:4). It pictures cleansing from sin (Acts 22:16). It marks entry into the body of Christ (1 Cor 12:13). And it is done in the name of the Triune God, placing the baptised person under his ownership and claim.

More than a personal testimony. Baptism is sometimes described as simply a public statement of someone's decision. It is a public confession, but it is more. It is God's covenant sign, administered by the church in his name, declaring his promise to all who believe and claiming them as his. It is about what God has done before it is about what we have done.

What baptism does not do. Baptism does not cause new birth. The thief on the cross was saved without it (Luke 23:43). Simon the magician was baptised without being saved (Acts 8:13, 20-23). Salvation is by grace through faith. Yet baptism is not therefore unimportant. A believer who refuses baptism is disobeying Christ.

Mode. Christians have baptised by immersion, pouring and sprinkling. Immersion best pictures burial and resurrection with Christ, and fits the New Testament descriptions of going down into the water and coming up out of it (Acts 8:38-39). But the meaning of baptism does not depend on the amount of water.
4.theology:
Who should be baptised? The views. Most of the historic Reformed tradition, along with Roman Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran and Anglican churches, baptises the infants of believers. Reformed paedobaptists argue from the unity of the covenant of grace: children of believers received the covenant sign of circumcision in the Old Testament, and baptism has replaced circumcision (Col 2:11-12). Whole households were baptised in Acts (Acts 16:15, 33). Reformed credobaptists hold that baptism is for those who profess faith, because the new covenant is made with those who know the Lord.

The verdict: Believer's baptism is the more faithful position. The new covenant promises that all its members shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest (Jer 31:34; Heb 8:11). Every baptism the New Testament describes follows repentance and faith, and the household baptisms do not mention infants; in one case the word was first spoken to all in the house, and the whole household rejoiced in God (Acts 16:32-34). Baptism signifies union with Christ by faith, which belongs to those who believe. Paedobaptists are dear brothers and sisters, and the Covenant Theology study sets out both cases more fully.

Children of believers: Children of Christian parents are greatly privileged. They hear the gospel, are prayed for and are raised in the church. They should be taught to trust Christ from their earliest days, and baptised when they credibly profess faith.
4.examples:
Then: An Ethiopian official was reading Isaiah 53 in his chariot when Philip explained it to him. As they came to some water, he asked, What prevents me from being baptized? They went down into the water, and Philip baptised him. The eunuch went on his way rejoicing (Acts 8:36-39). Faith, then baptism, then joy.

Now: A woman became a Christian in her forties, but has delayed baptism because she is shy and dreads standing in front of the church. Reading Matthew 28, she sees it as an act of obedience to Christ rather than a performance. On the day, her voice shakes as she confesses her faith. Afterwards, many in the church embrace her. She belongs.

A simple test: If you are a believer who has not been baptised, what is holding you back from obeying Christ in this?

verseByVerse.quote: And Jesus came and said to them, "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus' authority is the ground of the command. Making disciples includes baptising them and teaching them. Baptism marks the beginning of discipleship, not its end. And it is done in the one name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, bringing the believer into a relationship with the whole Trinity. The promise follows: Jesus will be with his people to the end.

verseByVerse.quote: And Peter said to them, "Repent and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is for you and for your children and for all who are far off, everyone whom the Lord our God calls to himself." And with many other words he bore witness and continued to exhort them, saying, "Save yourselves from this crooked generation." So those who received his word were baptized, and there were added that day about three thousand souls. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter's hearers were cut to the heart and asked what to do. He told them to repent and be baptised in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins. The promise of the Spirit is for them, their children and those far off, everyone whom the Lord our God calls to himself. Those who received his word were baptised. The order is consistent: hearing, believing, baptism.

verseByVerse.quote: Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life. For if we have been united with him in a death like his, we shall certainly be united with him in a resurrection like his. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul uses baptism to answer a question: should Christians keep sinning so that grace may abound? No, because in baptism we were united to Christ in his death and resurrection. Baptism marks the end of the old life and the beginning of the new. To return to sin is to deny what our baptism signifies.

verseByVerse.quote: In him also you were circumcised with a circumcision made without hands, by putting off the body of the flesh, by the circumcision of Christ, having been buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in the powerful working of God, who raised him from the dead. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul connects circumcision and baptism, but notice what kind of circumcision: one made without hands, the cutting away of the old nature by Christ. Believers have been buried with him in baptism and raised with him through faith. The spiritual reality comes through faith, and baptism signifies it.

4.reflection:
What does baptism mean according to Romans 6:3-5?

Why is baptism more than a personal testimony?

How would you explain your view on infant baptism to a Christian who disagrees, with grace?

If you have been baptised, how does remembering your baptism encourage you to live for Christ?

5.title: The Lord's Supper
5.overview:
On the night he was betrayed, Jesus took bread and wine and gave them a new meaning. This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me. And the cup: This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood (Luke 22:19-20). He gave his church a meal to keep until he returns.

A meal of remembrance. The Supper looks back. It calls us to remember Christ's death, not as a distant historical event but as the sacrifice by which we are saved. For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes (1 Cor 11:26).

A meal of communion. The Supper looks up. The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a participation in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a participation in the body of Christ? (1 Cor 10:16). In the Supper believers truly feed on Christ by faith. It is not only a visual aid; it is a means of grace, through which the Spirit strengthens our faith and deepens our union with Christ.

A meal of fellowship. The Supper looks around. Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread (1 Cor 10:17). It is a family meal. Divisions and contempt for other believers contradict what the meal declares, which is why Paul rebuked the Corinthians so severely for humiliating poorer members at the table (1 Cor 11:20-22).

A meal of hope. The Supper looks forward. Jesus said he would not drink the fruit of the vine again until the kingdom comes (Luke 22:18). Every Lord's Supper is a foretaste of the marriage supper of the Lamb (Rev 19:9).

Coming worthily. Paul warns against eating in an unworthy manner (1 Cor 11:27). This does not mean that only those who feel worthy may come. No one is worthy. It means coming without discerning the body, with careless contempt for Christ and his people, or with unrepented sin. Let a person examine himself, then, and so eat (1 Cor 11:28). The Supper is for repentant sinners, not for the perfect.
5.theology:
How is Christ present? The views. Roman Catholic teaching holds that the bread and wine become the actual body and blood of Christ (transubstantiation) and that the Mass is a sacrifice. Lutherans hold that Christ's body and blood are present "in, with and under" the bread and wine. Many evangelicals hold that the Supper is a memorial only, a reminder of Christ's death. The Reformed view holds that Christ is truly present by his Spirit, and believers truly feed on him by faith, while the bread and wine remain bread and wine.

The verdict: The Reformed view fits the whole of Scripture. "This is my body" is like "I am the door": a sign that represents a reality. Christ's body is now in heaven (Acts 3:21), and his sacrifice was once for all (Heb 10:10), so it cannot be repeated in a Mass. Yet Paul calls the Supper a real participation in Christ (1 Cor 10:16), more than a memory. Christ meets his people at his table by his Spirit, and faith receives him.

Who may come? The Supper is for baptised believers who are walking in repentance. Children who have not yet professed faith, and unbelievers, should not take it, though they may be present and should be lovingly taught what it means.
5.examples:
Then: On the evening of the resurrection, two disciples walked to Emmaus with a stranger. At supper, he took the bread and blessed and broke it and gave it to them. And their eyes were opened, and they recognized him (Luke 24:30-31). Christ makes himself known in the breaking of bread.

Now: A believer has always found communion awkward. She is not sure what to think about, and often wonders if she is worthy enough. Her pastor explains that the Supper is not a test of worthiness but a gift for the weak. Next time, she confesses her sins, looks to Christ crucified and risen, and receives the bread and cup as his gift to her. For the first time, it feels like a meal.

A simple test: When you take the Lord's Supper, do you come as someone performing a ritual or as someone being fed by Christ?

verseByVerse.quote: And when the hour came, he reclined at table, and the apostles with him. And he said to them, "I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer. For I tell you I will not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God." And he took a cup, and when he had given thanks he said, "Take this, and divide it among yourselves. For I tell you that from now on I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes." And he took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and gave it to them, saying, "This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me." And likewise the cup after they had eaten, saying, "This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus ate the Passover with his disciples, the meal that remembered Israel's rescue from Egypt by the blood of a lamb. Now he gives it a new focus: his own body given and blood poured out. The new covenant promised by Jeremiah is established by his death. Every Lord's Supper remembers a greater exodus.

verseByVerse.quote: The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a participation in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a participation in the body of Christ? Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul uses the Lord's Supper to warn against idolatry. Those who share the Lord's table cannot also share in idol feasts. His argument assumes that the Supper is a real participation in Christ, not a mere symbol. And it binds believers together: one bread, one body.

verseByVerse.quote: For I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night when he was betrayed took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it, and said, "This is my body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of me." In the same way also he took the cup, after supper, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me." For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul hands on what he received from the Lord. These are among the oldest written words about the Supper. Notice the emphasis on remembrance and proclamation. Every time the church eats and drinks, it preaches the gospel. And the Supper carries a horizon: until he comes.

verseByVerse.quote: Whoever, therefore, eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty concerning the body and blood of the Lord. Let a person examine himself, then, and so eat of the bread and drink of the cup. For anyone who eats and drinks without discerning the body eats and drinks judgment on himself. That is why many of you are weak and ill, and some have died. But if we judged ourselves truly, we would not be judged. But when we are judged by the Lord, we are disciplined so that we may not be condemned along with the world. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Corinthians were taking the Supper while despising poorer members. Paul says this was eating unworthily, and that God had disciplined some with sickness and death. Self-examination is the remedy. And even God's discipline has a loving purpose: so that we may not be condemned along with the world.

5.reflection:
What do the four directions of the Supper (back, up, around, forward) teach you about it?

What does it mean to take the Supper "in an unworthy manner"?

How would you explain the Reformed view of Christ's presence in the Supper?

How can you prepare your heart before the next Lord's Supper?

6.title: Purity, Unity and Mission
6.overview:
Every healthy church needs three things held together: purity, unity and mission. Without purity, unity becomes compromise. Without unity, purity becomes harshness. And without mission, both turn inward.

Purity: church discipline. Church discipline is the loving correction of members who persist in serious sin. It begins privately and gently: Brothers, if anyone is caught in any transgression, you who are spiritual should restore him in a spirit of gentleness (Gal 6:1). If a member refuses to repent of serious, public sin, Jesus and Paul teach that the church must finally remove him from membership (Matt 18:17; 1 Cor 5:13). This sounds harsh, but its aims are loving: to bring the sinner to repentance (1 Cor 5:5), to protect the church from spreading sin (1 Cor 5:6) and to guard Christ's honour before the world. And the door is always open: when a disciplined person repents, the church must forgive and welcome him back (2 Cor 2:7-8).

Unity: keeping the peace. Paul urges believers to be eager to maintain the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace (Eph 4:3). Unity is not uniformity, and it is not achieved by ignoring truth. It is built on the one faith (Eph 4:4-6). But within that faith, Christians must bear with one another's differences, weaknesses and preferences. Jesus prayed that his people would be one, so that the world may believe that you have sent me (John 17:21). Church unity is evangelistic.

Mission: the church sent. The church exists not only for itself but for the world. Christ has given it the task of making disciples of all nations. This happens through faithful preaching, through members speaking of Christ in their daily lives, through supporting missionaries and planting churches, and through deeds of love that adorn the gospel (Titus 2:10).

Growing up together. God gives the church teachers to equip the saints for the work of ministry, so that the whole body grows to maturity, speaking the truth in love (Eph 4:12, 15). A mature church is not one with a famous pastor, but one in which every member is growing and serving.
6.theology:
Discipline is not punishment: The church does not punish sin; Christ has borne the punishment for his people. Discipline is a warning and a call to come back. It treats sin as seriously as God does and the sinner as lovingly as God does.

Secondary differences: Christians must distinguish between first-order truths (the gospel, the Trinity, the person of Christ), which define the faith; second-order matters (such as baptism and church government), which may require separate churches; and third-order matters (such as music style or details about the end times), which should never divide a church.

The church will be perfected: The church on earth is flawed and often disappointing. But Christ is sanctifying her, and one day she will be presented without spot or wrinkle (Eph 5:27). Love the church as she is because of what Christ will make her.
6.examples:
Then: In Corinth, a man was living with his father's wife, and the church was proud of its tolerance. Paul commanded discipline. In his next letter Paul speaks of a disciplined man, perhaps the same one, who had repented, and he urged the church to forgive and comfort him and reaffirm your love for him (2 Cor 2:7-8). Discipline worked as it was meant to.

Now: A church disagrees bitterly over a change in worship style. Some threaten to leave. The elders call the church to read Ephesians 4:1-16 together, to repent of harsh words and to remember what unites them. The disagreement is not fully resolved, but people choose to bear with one another, and the church stays together.

A simple test: Are you more likely to break the unity of your church by insisting on your preferences, or to weaken its purity by avoiding hard conversations?

verseByVerse.quote: Brothers, if anyone is caught in any transgression, you who are spiritual should restore him in a spirit of gentleness. Keep watch on yourself, lest you too be tempted. Bear one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Restoring a fallen brother is the work of the spiritual, and it must be done in a spirit of gentleness. And those who restore must watch themselves, lest they too be tempted. Bearing one another's burdens fulfils the law of Christ. Discipline begins not with a church meeting but with one believer gently helping another.

verseByVerse.quote: When you are assembled in the name of the Lord Jesus and my spirit is present, with the power of our Lord Jesus, you are to deliver this man to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord. Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump? Cleanse out the old leaven that you may be a new lump, as you really are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed. Let us therefore celebrate the festival, not with the old leaven, the leaven of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The church was to act together, in the name of the Lord Jesus, to remove an unrepentant man. Paul's goal is that his spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord. He also gives a warning: a little leaven leavens the whole lump. Tolerated sin spreads. Christ our Passover has been sacrificed; the church must live as his holy people.

verseByVerse.quote: I therefore, a prisoner for the Lord, urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling to which you have been called, with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love, eager to maintain the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. There is one body and one Spirit—just as you were called to the one hope that belongs to your call— one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul begs believers to walk worthy of their calling with humility, gentleness and patience. Unity is already given by the Spirit; our job is to maintain it. And it rests on seven great "ones": one body, one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father. Christian unity is anchored in truth.

verseByVerse.quote: "I do not ask for these only, but also for those who will believe in me through their word, that they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me. The glory that you have given me I have given to them, that they may be one even as we are one, I in them and you in me, that they may become perfectly one, so that the world may know that you sent me and loved them even as you loved me. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus prays for all who will believe through the apostles' word. That includes us. He prays that they will be one as the Father and Son are one. The goal is mission: that the world may know that the Father sent the Son and loves his people. Divided churches undermine their witness. United churches commend the gospel.

6.reflection:
Why is church discipline an act of love? How can it go wrong?

Read Ephesians 4:1-16. What does it say about the unity and maturity of the church?

Which matters should never divide a church? Which may require separate churches?

What is one way you could strengthen the unity or mission of your church this month?
